items.title: Why a private chat 404s for a signed-out visitor
items.body:
`loadChatWithMessages` returns `null` when `chat.visibility === 'private'` and there is no `userId` (or the user is not the owner). `SearchPage` checks `if (!chat) notFound()` first, so the visitor gets the 404 page. The next check, `private && !userId` leading to `redirect('/auth/login')`, can never see a private chat without a user, so the redirect is effectively dead code. The real-code-patterns page describes the redirect; the senior page lists the 404 as a known symptom; the code decides.

- *Redirect to /auth/login*: unreachable here, because notFound() runs first.
- *Read-only render*: private chats are not readable by others.
- *Empty Chat*: the page never renders when loadChat returns null.

items.title: Concept: small routes, auth modes and row-level security
items.body:
**Feedback route.** `app/api/feedback/route.ts` validates its JSON body by hand, one `if` at a time. List the checks in order with the response each one returns, and note which later steps (Langfuse, the database) sit behind which check.

**Auth modes.** `lib/auth/get-current-user.ts` supports a mode with authentication switched off for personal Docker deployments. Read the branch for `ENABLE_AUTH === 'false'` and the guard inside it, and work out what identity a request gets in that mode.

**Row-level security.** Postgres RLS policies in `lib/db/schema.ts` compare a row's `user_id` with `current_setting('app.current_user_id', true)`. `lib/db/with-rls.ts` sets that value at the start of a transaction with `set_config`. Look up the third parameter of `set_config` in the PostgreSQL docs.

**Uploads from the browser.** `hooks/use-file-dropzone.ts` filters files, checks a maximum count and posts each file to `/api/upload`. Compare the fields it reads from the response with the object the upload route returns.

excerpts.quote: RLS: PostgreSQL Row Level Security; this repo uses policies and `set_config`.

readMore.why: Tests that pin how withRLS and withOptionalRLS call the database.

items.title: Why dropping two more files uploads nothing
items.body:
handleDrop computes `total = uploadedFiles.length + allowed.length`, here 2 + 2 = 4. Because that is greater than `maxFiles` (3), it shows "You can upload a maximum of 3 files." and returns before creating any upload entries. The `slice(0, maxFiles)` further down is only reached when the total fits.

- *Uploads the first, drops the other*: the hook does not pick a subset; it stops.
- *Uploads both, then trims*: the return comes before any upload starts.
- *Replaces the older attachments*: existing files are never removed here.

excerpts.quote: toast.error(`You can upload a maximum of ${maxFiles} files.`)

items.title: When the streamed answer is lost
items.body:
A fallback error that is not a duplicate key takes the `else` branch: the code logs "Fallback chat creation failed" and `return`s. The `upsertMessage` call and its retry come later in the function, so they never run. The user already saw the answer on screen, but it is not stored. This is the swallow-and-log risk the real-code-patterns page warns about.

- *Saved through the retry helper*: the retry wraps the message upsert, which is never reached.
- *Saved to a guest table*: guest chats are never persisted, and there is no such table.
- *Rethrown as a 500*: the response is already streaming; the helper only logs.

items.title: Why everyone shares one id when auth is off
items.body:
With authentication disabled on a non-cloud deployment, `getCurrentUserId` returns `process.env.ANONYMOUS_USER_ID || 'anonymous-user'`. Without the variable both browsers get the literal `anonymous-user`, so they see and change the same chats. The warning printed at startup says so: all users share the same user ID.

- *Random id per cookie*: no id is generated or stored.
- *undefined, treated as guests*: the branch returns a string, so requests count as signed in.
- *Supabase anonymous sessions*: Supabase is not consulted in this mode.

items.title: Concept: loading a saved chat and saving a streamed one
items.body:
Two paths move a chat between the database and the screen.

**Loading.** `app/search/[id]/page.tsx` is a Server Component. It calls `loadChat` in `lib/actions/chat.ts`, which wraps `loadChatWithMessages` in `lib/db/actions.ts` with Next.js `unstable_cache`. Read the cache key, the tags and the revalidate option, and think about what a stale entry would look like. Then read `loadChatWithMessages` completely, including its permission check, and compare it with the checks in the page. Ask which check runs first for each kind of visitor.

**Saving.** An authenticated answer is streamed first and saved afterwards. In `lib/streaming/create-chat-stream-response.ts`, find `onFinish` and note its first line. Then read `lib/streaming/helpers/persist-stream-results.ts` in order: the title promise, the pending initial save and its fallback, the message upsert with retry, and the title update. For every `catch`, write down whether the function continues or returns.

excerpts.quote: The stream can render immediately while persistence happens at completion.

readMore.why: The whole persistence helper; short enough to read in one sitting.

items.title: Why score 0 is rejected with 400
items.body:
The route reads `traceId` and `score` from the JSON body. traceId `"t1"` passes the first check. The second check rejects any score that is not exactly 1 or -1, so 0 returns 400 with "score must be 1 (good) or -1 (bad)".

- *200 recorded*: the request never gets past validation.
- *400 traceId is required*: traceId is present.
- *422 with Zod issues*: the route validates by hand; no Zod schema is involved.

excerpts.quote: return new Response('score must be 1 (good) or -1 (bad)', {

items.title: The upload response shape mismatch
items.body:
After a successful upload the hook stores `uploaded.url`, `uploaded.name` and `uploaded.key`. The upload route returns `filename`, `url`, `mediaType` and `type`; there is no `name` or `key`. So the stored name is `undefined`, which matches the mid-level mission's hint and the senior page's bug symptom.

- *Read from uploaded.filename*: the hook never reads filename.
- *The R2 key as name*: the route does not return the key at all.
- *Sanitized name*: the route returns the original file.name as filename, and the hook does not read it.

items.title: Why an aborted answer is not saved
items.body:
`onFinish` receives `isAborted`. Its first statement after the timing log is `if (isAborted || !responseMessage) return`, so `persistStreamResults` does not run and the partial answer is not written. The `finally` block still flushes Langfuse.

- *Saved with an aborted flag*: no flag is written; nothing is written.
- *Saved as is*: that would require reaching persistStreamResults.
- *Queued for the next request*: there is no queue for unsaved answers.

items.title: Why cloud deployments cannot disable auth
items.body:
In the `ENABLE_AUTH === 'false'` branch, the first statement checks `MORPHIC_CLOUD_DEPLOYMENT === 'true'` and throws "ENABLE_AUTH=false is not allowed in MORPHIC_CLOUD_DEPLOYMENT". A shared cloud deployment is not allowed to collapse every visitor into one identity.

- *anonymous-user with a warning*: that is the non-cloud path, after the guard.
- *Ask Supabase*: the function does not fall through to Supabase in this branch.
- *undefined*: undefined is what a signed-out visitor gets when auth is enabled.

excerpts.quote: ENABLE_AUTH=false is not allowed in MORPHIC_CLOUD_DEPLOYMENT

items.title: Start here: the docs-codex-learning track for Morphic
items.body:
Morphic is an open-source AI answer engine built on Next.js, the Vercel AI SDK, Drizzle and Supabase. This quest uses the `morphic/docs-codex-learning/` track, which has four sub-tracks. Read these three pages:

1. `technology-best-practices/02-real-code-patterns.md`: per technology, where it is used, a best-practice example with a file path and line range, and a weak or risky pattern.
2. `architectural-cartographer/01-junior-engineer.md`: the folder map, three backend anatomies and a glossary.
3. `mission-learning-path/02-tier-2-mid-level-missions.md`: missions with a goal, files to open and Socratic questions.

`architectural-cartographer/00-reading-map.md` gives a good order for opening the code itself.

The guides quote short code snippets; the quiz is about what the full functions do with specific inputs. For every snippet, open the cited file and read the lines around it, especially early `return` statements and `catch` blocks. Several mission questions ("What does proxy.ts do when Supabase is not configured?") are worth answering in writing before you start the quiz.

excerpts.quote: Boundaries are layered locks: middleware refreshes session, auth resolves user, RLS constrains DB access.

readMore.why: A file-by-file reading order through the codebase.

items.title: What a failed title generation leaves behind
items.body:
For a new chat, `generateChatTitle` runs in parallel and its `.catch` returns `DEFAULT_CHAT_TITLE` ("Untitled"). In `persistStreamResults`, the title update runs only when `chatTitle && chatTitle !== DEFAULT_CHAT_TITLE`, so no update happens and the chat keeps the title it was created with.

- *First 50 characters*: 50 characters is how the page metadata trims an existing title; no code derives a title from the message here.
- *Empty string*: the fallback is the Untitled constant, not an empty string.
- *Rolled back*: a title error is caught; nothing is rolled back.

items.title: How loadChat is cached
items.body:
`getCachedChatWithMessages` builds an `unstable_cache` around the database call. The cache key includes the chat id and the requesting user id (or `anonymous`), so each requesting user gets an entry of its own. The entry is tagged `chat-<id>` and `chat` and revalidates after 60 seconds; actions that change a chat call `revalidateTag` to drop it sooner.

- *Module-level Map until restart*: there is no Map; Next.js manages the cache and expires it.
- *React cache() per request*: cache() is not used; entries outlive a request.
- *No caching*: the function exists precisely to cache the load.

items.title: Why disabled tracing skips the database too
items.body:
Right after validation the route checks `isTracingEnabled()`. When it is false it returns 200 "Feedback tracking is not enabled". The Langfuse score and the `updateMessageFeedback` call both come later in the function, so the message metadata is not updated even though a messageId was sent. Whether that coupling is intended is a fair review question.

- *Score written, Langfuse skipped*: the DB write sits after the tracing check, so it is skipped as well.
- *503*: the route answers 200 in this case.
- *Queued in memory*: there is no queue.

excerpts.quote: return new Response('Feedback tracking is not enabled', {

items.title: Why a duplicate key on the fallback is fine
items.body:
If the pending initial save rejects, persistStreamResults tries `createChatWithFirstMessage` again. When that fallback throws an error whose message contains "duplicate key" or "unique constraint", the chat must already exist, so the code logs "Chat already exists" and carries on to save the assistant message.

- *Returns without saving*: that is what happens for any other fallback error.
- *Rethrows*: nothing in this helper rethrows; it logs.
- *Deletes and recreates*: no delete is attempted.

excerpts.quote: Chat already exists, this is fine - continue to save the response message

items.title: What the true in set_config does
items.body:
PostgreSQL's `set_config(setting, value, is_local)` with `is_local = true` acts like `SET LOCAL`: the value lasts until the current transaction ends. withRLS calls it inside `db.transaction`, so the user id is visible to the RLS policies for that transaction only, and a pooled connection does not carry it into another user's request. The comment in the file says the same.

- *Whole DB session*: that is what false would mean.
- *Checked against a users table*: set_config only sets a value; it checks nothing.
- *Creates the policy*: the policies are defined in the schema and migrations.

excerpts.quote: Using SET LOCAL ensures it's only valid for this transaction
